audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL state trie specification (patricialize function) does not apply to CL consensus client (Prysm/Go). Prysm implements Merkle tries for beacon state, not Ethereum execution layer state tries.

Component mismatch: EL state trie specification (patricialize with Account/Receipt/Uint types) does not apply to CL consensus client (Prysm/Go). Prysm does not implement EL state/transaction/receipt tries.
Component mismatch: EL trie root() function returning 32-byte roots is an execution layer specification. Prysm implements beacon state hash tree roots using SSZ, not EL Patricia-Merkle tries.

Component mismatch: Unsecured tries (transactions, receipts) are EL components. Prysm as a CL client does not implement or process EL tries directly. DoS concerns for EL tries are not applicable to CL beacon state processing.
Component mismatch: encode_node isinstance chain and previous_trie references are from EL Python specification. Prysm uses Go and SSZ encoding for consensus state, not EL fork-aware trie encoding.
Component mismatch: Unbounded state entry growth via SSTORE/CREATE is an EL concern (execution layer state trie). Prysm processes beacon state with fixed-size structures, not EL world state.
Component mismatch: root() hashing small RLP-encoded nodes is EL trie specification. Prysm uses SSZ for beacon state merkleization, not RLP encoding or EL trie root computation.
Component mismatch: _prepare_trie processing trie._data is from EL Python specification. Prysm does not implement this function or the EL trie data structures.
Component mismatch: Secured trie key hashing (keccak256) for state/storage is EL specification. Prysm uses SSZ hash tree roots for beacon state, not keccak256-based secured tries.

Component mismatch: Trie root computation independence from trie._data.items() iteration order is EL Python specification concern. Prysm uses deterministic SSZ merkleization, not dict-based trie structures.
